about: At Daimler Truck Innovation Center India (DTICI) in Bengaluru, I scaled fleet Spark ETL scripts originally written for 50 vehicles to 175k+ capacity (~70,000 live trucks) and replaced dedicated Power BI servers with a FastAPI + React Databricks app that loads ~3x faster at less than half the compute spend.

Outside work, I solo-built the bilingual FiT-UC Flutter app on Google Play for Udayan Care NGO—saving ₹1,00,000+ in build quotes and ~30% field Excel time—hosted on a consolidated Proxmox VE 8 Linux server that also runs a 6-node K3s lab.

bulletPoints: Replaced dedicated Power BI capacity with a cached FastAPI + React Databricks app, making loads ~3x faster, UI shipping 3-4x quicker, and compute spend 50%+ lower.
Verified Python and C++ OTA collection scripts on hardware test rigs prior to fleet rollout across ~70,000 connected trucks.
Avoided ₹1,00,000+ in agency build quotes and ₹2,000-5,000/mo cloud bills by developing FiT-UC solo with AI workflows and self-hosting NocoDB + Node.js on Proxmox LXC.
Reduced manual Excel entry roughly 30% for 5-6 field coordinators serving 20-30 monthly active users on Google Play across 3 modules: courses, mentor booking, and Gotify alerts.
Refactored duplicate Spark and SQL ETL scripts originally meant for 50 vehicles so pipelines scaled past a 10x wall to 175k+ tested vehicle capacity across ~70,000 live trucks.
Simplified lookup tables and lightweight Delta views to clear 10x scale Power BI refresh bottlenecks before moving full-time into software engineering.
Scripted Python regression checks saving roughly 1 hour/day and benchmarked GPU SAT solvers at 10x higher constraint difficulty.
Delivered 1 executive Power BI report alongside ~70% accurate staffing forecasts trained with Facebook Prophet in Python.
Fixed ARM Linux cross-compilation and dependency issues to get the Alexa Voice SDK running on 1 Raspberry Pi smart-mirror prototype.
Owned 1 end-to-end Apache Superset dashboard and supported 3 civic analytics projects unifying SQL, Kobo Toolbox, Glide Apps, and AppSheet.

evolution.title: Debian, Kali & Alpine on Repurposed Laptops
evolution.summary: Before trying hypervisors, I ran bare-metal Debian, Kali Linux, and Alpine Linux across spare laptops, running self-hosted services by hand with Docker Engine and Docker Compose.
learnings: Managed Linux networking, firewalls, systemd services, and volume permissions by hand.
Used Alpine for small production containers, Debian for stable hosts, and Kali for local network debugging.

evolution.stage: Phase 02 · 3-Node HA Proxmox Cluster + 4th Laptop PBS
evolution.title: Distributed Proxmox VE Quorum & Proxmox Backup Server
evolution.summary: Switched to Proxmox VE and rebuilt the 4-laptop stack into a 3-node High-Availability (HA) PVE cluster with a dedicated 4th laptop acting as Proxmox Backup Server (PBS).
learnings: Practiced Corosync quorum voting, split-brain prevention, HA failover groups, and live VM migration across nodes.
Set up Proxmox Backup Server (PBS) for deduplicated backups, retention policies, and restore drills.
Learned Linux bridges (vmbr0), thin storage pools, and LXC vs KVM trade-offs.
evolution.stack: Proxmox VE · Proxmox Backup Server (PBS) · Corosync HA · LXC · KVM

evolution.stage: Phase 03 · Consolidated PVE 8 Host & K3s Cluster

evolution.summary: Consolidated the 4-laptop setup onto one primary Proxmox VE 8 server for lower power draw and shared memory, hosting NGO containers alongside a 6-node K3s lab.
learnings: Runs live Udayan Care NGO containers (NocoDB LXC, Node.js Auth at udayan.diivvansh.com, Gotify alerts).
Runs a nested 6-node K3s cluster (3 masters + 3 workers) with MetalLB VIPs and Traefik ingress exposed via Cloudflare Tunnels and Tailscale.

faqs.question: Who is Divansh Prasad and what does he build?
faqs.answer: Divansh Prasad is a Software Engineer at Daimler Truck Innovation Center India (DTICI) in Bengaluru working on Databricks Apache Spark ETL pipelines across ~70,000 connected commercial trucks, FastAPI and React internal web applications, and Over-The-Air (OTA) vehicle telemetry workflows validated on hardware test rigs.

faqs.question: What volunteer software and mobile apps has Divansh Prasad shipped?
faqs.answer: Outside work, Divansh volunteers as Lead Developer for Udayan Care NGO, where he built and shipped the bilingual (English and Hindi) FiT-UC Flutter mobile app live on Google Play Store backed by self-hosted NocoDB and Node.js authentication containers on Proxmox VE.

faqs.question: How is Divansh Prasad's self-hosted Proxmox and K3s infrastructure designed?
faqs.answer: His homelab evolved from bare-metal Debian, Kali, and Alpine Linux hosts running Docker Compose to a 3-node Proxmox VE HA cluster with a dedicated 4th Proxmox Backup Server (PBS) laptop, and consolidated onto a Proxmox VE 8 host running production LXC containers and a 6-node K3s cluster with MetalLB Layer-2 VIP, Traefik ingress, Tailscale, and Cloudflare Tunnels.
